title: Area and Perimeter of an Equilateral Triangle as Functions of Side Length
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Express the area A and perimeter p of an equilateral triangle as functions of the triangle's side length x.

steps.title: Express the Perimeter in Terms of x
steps.explanation: An equilateral triangle has three sides of equal length x, so its perimeter p is the sum of the three sides, 3x.
steps.why: The perimeter of any polygon is the sum of the lengths of its boundary edges.

steps.title: Find the Altitude Using the Pythagorean Theorem
steps.explanation: Dropping an altitude of length h from one vertex to the opposite side bisects that side into two segments of length x/2. Applying the Pythagorean theorem to one of the resulting right triangles yields h = (sqrt(3)/2)x.
steps.why: In an equilateral triangle, the altitude to the base is also the perpendicular bisector of the base.

steps.title: Compute the Area Function A(x)
steps.explanation: Substitute the base x and height (sqrt(3)/2)x into the standard triangle area formula A = (1/2)bh to obtain A(x) = (sqrt(3)/4)x^2.
steps.why: The area of any triangle equals half the product of its base length and corresponding altitude.
